sentences[0].english: How are you? – I'm fine, thanks.
sentences[0].why: gehen + es works on the dative: ich → mir — 'it goes well TO me'.
sentences[1].why: Wie geht es…? takes the dative: du → dir.
sentences[2].why: Formal Sie in the dative is Ihnen — always capital.
sentences[3].why: helfen always takes the dative: ich → mir — you help TO someone in German.
sentences[4].why: gehören takes the dative: er → ihm — it belongs TO him.
sentences[5].why: sie ('she') in the dative is ihr.
sentences[6].why: danken takes the dative: formal Sie → Ihnen — you give thanks TO someone.
sentences[7].why: gefallen takes the dative: dir — the picture is pleasing TO you.
sentences[8].why: helfen + dative: wir → uns — uns doubles as accusative and dative.
sentences[9].why: ihr (you all) in the dative is euch — same form as the accusative.
sentences[10].why: sie ('they') in the dative is ihnen — small i; capital Ihnen is the formal you.
sentences[11].english: The child is ill. It is not well.
sentences[11].why: es in the dative is ihm — the same form as er takes.
sentences[12].english: The teacher explains the rule to us.
sentences[12].why: The person you explain TO is dative: uns — the rule itself is the accusative.
sentences[13].why: zeigen: the ones shown TO are dative — euch.
help.intro: Wie geht es dir? — how are you? — is one of the first questions you learn, and the dir in it is a dative pronoun. For now you need exactly this much dative: the pronouns mir, dir, ihm, ihr, uns, euch, ihnen, Ihnen after a handful of verbs that always take them — helfen (help), danken (thank), gehören (belong to), gefallen (please, i.e. 'like'), and the phrase es geht. The full dative — articles, nouns, prepositions — comes later in the course. For now these are chunks: Kannst du mir helfen? Das gehört mir. Gefällt dir das? Ich danke Ihnen. Notice that ihr is now 'to her' and ihnen 'to them', and Ihnen with a capital is the formal you.
help.tips[0].title: The dative pronouns
help.tips[0].text: mir, dir, ihm, ihr, ihm, uns, euch, ihnen, Ihnen. mir and dir rhyme; ihm is his/its, ihr is hers; ihnen is them, Ihnen is you (formal).
help.tips[0].check.q: Formal: How are you, Mrs Lang? Wie geht es ____, Frau Lang?
help.tips[0].check.why: es geht takes the dative, and the formal you in the dative is Ihnen.
help.tips[1].title: The verbs that want them
help.tips[1].text: helfen, danken, gehören, gefallen, gratulieren, antworten — the person after them is dative: Ich helfe dir. Ich danke Ihnen. Das gehört mir.
help.tips[1].trap: English 'help me' and 'see me' use the same 'me'. German uses mich after sehen but mir after helfen; the verb decides.
help.tips[1].check.q: I thank him for the flowers: Ich danke ____ für die Blumen.
help.tips[1].check.why: danken always takes the dative, so 'him' is ihm, not the accusative ihn.
help.tips[2].title: gefallen turns the sentence round
help.tips[2].text: 'I like the picture' is Das Bild gefällt mir — the picture pleases me. The thing is the subject; the person is dative.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Do you like the flat? – Yes, I like it a lot.
help.tips[2].check.q: I like the shoes: Die Schuhe gefallen ____.
help.tips[2].check.why: With gefallen the shoes are the subject and the person who likes them is dative: mir.
help.tips[2].visual.rows[0].note: The film is the subject; mir is the person it pleases.
help.tips[3].title: mir/dir for how you are, mich/dich for what is seen
help.tips[3].text: es geht mir, hilf mir, danke dir → dative. sieh mich, liebe dich → accusative. This first dative is small: learn its verbs and it can't go wrong.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: I love you (acc.) and I help you (dat.).
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: Can you see me? – Yes, and I'll help you in a moment.
help.tips[3].check.q: Informal, 'I'll see you tomorrow': Ich sehe ____ morgen.
help.tips[3].check.why: sehen is not one of the dative verbs, so it takes the accusative dich.
help.remember[0]: helfen, danken, gehören, gefallen, es geht — five triggers, all take mir/dir/Ihnen.
help.remember[1]: ihr = to her, ihnen = to them, Ihnen = to you — the h and the capital are the clues.
help.context.en: Good morning, Mrs Klein, how are you? – Fine, thanks. And you? – I'm fine too. Can you help me a moment? This bag isn't mine. – It belongs to him, the new colleague. – Ah, thank you!
help.mistakes[0].why: es geht takes the dative pronoun.
help.hook: Ask how someone is, offer help, thank them and say what you like: mir, dir and Ihnen make it all work.
